claim_text: Arm-A training increases exact activation sparsity: x zero fraction grows from 0.499 at canonical init to 0.651 at step 2k and 0.752 at step 19,074; RoPE-pair zero fraction grows from 0.452 to 0.597; u=x*y zero fraction from 0.749 to 0.947.
dataset: 4 trained checkpoints of ONE Arm-A 2.5B trajectory + canonical-init control; 16 synthetic packed windows per checkpoint (4 batches x 4 rows x 2048 tokens), random tokens
metric: mean zero fraction across 32 (level,head) cells, counted over 32768 tokens per checkpoint
uncertainty: per-cell spread p10-p90 reported in sparsity_maturation.json; init value is deterministic; sampling noise of zero fractions at n=32768 tokens is <0.01
confound_checks: canonical random-init control uses identical data/capture; position/level/head stratification (position_confounds.json) shows no sign reversal; y zero fraction moves the OTHER way (-0.030)
null_test: random-init calibration (E1): init zero fractions 0.499/0.749 are the architectural ReLU baseline
contradicting_evidence: absolute sparsity depends on synthetic token distribution; frozen-corpus values may differ (E3 pending)
paper_safe_wording: On synthetic packed windows from the trained trajectory, exact zero fractions increased by ~10 points for x and ~15 points for RoPE pairs relative to initialization; this is an E2 diagnostic pending frozen-corpus replication.
next_test: E3 frozen-corpus census (analysis/arm_a_science/E3_README.md)

claim_text: Training creates population-level concentration far beyond initialization: coordinate mass Gini rises 0.192->0.675 (x) and 0.597->0.805 (u); effective population N_eff/K falls 0.927->0.417 (x) and 0.522->0.207 (u).
dataset: same as S1
metric: Gini / exp-entropy / participation ratio of per-(level,head) global coordinate mass vectors
uncertainty: per-cell min/max in sparsity_maturation.json
confound_checks: init control; x and u move consistently; y does not (N_eff/K 0.353->0.390)
null_test: canonical-init calibration
contradicting_evidence: top-1% mass share for x barely moves (0.074->0.080) even though Gini rises strongly
paper_safe_wording: Most of the learned concentration is in the broad mass distribution, not the single top coordinate; the top-1% x share is nearly training-invariant.
next_test: E3 census; per-coordinate tracking over training

claim_text: Per-token u=x*y activation mass is strongly conditional: the token's own top-64 coordinates capture 0.784 of its u mass on average, while a frozen cross-fitted global top-64 captures only 0.362 (delta 0.421; all 32 level-head cells have delta>0.05 with per-cell range 0.190-0.516).
dataset: latest checkpoint; 4096 sampled tokens per level (4 batches x 4 rows x 2 chunks x 128 tokens), cross-fitted by batch split
metric: M_local(N) minus M_global(N), paired per token, N=64 per head (K=4096)
uncertainty: document-level block bootstrap per cell in topn_global_local.json (e.g. level-4 pooled x delta CI [0.0105, 0.0157] at N=256 with 15 documents); per-cell ranges given above
confound_checks: position strata (delta 0.083-0.129 at N=64 for x; 0.18-0.26 at N=256) do not explain the gap; data modes (mixed/single/heavy) all show it; random-init control delta is only 0.178 at N=64 and rises to 0.42 with training
null_test: uniform baseline N/K=0.0156 at N=64; random-init control
contradicting_evidence: M_global is itself far above uniform (0.362 vs 0.0156), so a substantial global skew coexists with the conditional component
paper_safe_wording: For u, per-context top-64 sets differ enough that a single global ranking captures less than half the mass that per-token rankings do.
next_test: E3 frozen-corpus replication; intervention comparing static vs dynamic routing at matched active compute

claim_text: The conditional component is much weaker for the pre-activation x than for u: x delta at N=64 is 0.092 (mean over cells) and 0.201 at N=1024, versus u 0.421 and 0.118; at the extreme top (N=16) x delta is 0.034.
dataset: same as S3
metric: per-cell M_local-M_global means across 32 cells at each N
effect_size: x is 3-5x more globally concentrated than u at small N; the gap ordering reverses only at N=1024 where both are near saturation
uncertainty: per-cell min/max in topn_global_local.json
confound_checks: level 7 is the exception with x delta 0.191 at N=1024; pooled-head x delta at 4096 is 0.134
null_test: uniform N/K; cross-fitting prevents in-sample optimism
contradicting_evidence: x is not purely static: at N=1024 all 32 cells have delta>0.05
paper_safe_wording: Input-side x has a stable global backbone with a smaller conditional component; the conditional structure is amplified in the multiplicative u path.
next_test: attribute the conditional component to x vs y via top-N set intersection (y top-64 identity sets are not stored yet)

claim_text: The population is FAST-conditional, not slow-conditional: top-64 Jaccard between same-document tokens one step apart (0.163 for x, 0.133 for u) is barely larger than between tokens from different documents (0.139 x, 0.097 u); the lag curve is flat from lag 1 to lag 127; Spearman rank correlation over all coordinates is high and flat (0.70 x, 0.85 u).
dataset: latest checkpoint; 32 sampled token pairs per lag category per (level,head,key), pairs within document for lags and across rows for the control
metric: mean top-N Jaccard, support Jaccard, Spearman, RBO
uncertainty: pair-level spread reported in population_stability.json cells (p10-p90)
confound_checks: rank correlation is high and flat, so the low Jaccard is not absence of structure but identity rotation; support Jaccard is also flat (0.36 x, 0.15 u)
null_test: cross-document pairs as the unrelated-context baseline; random-init Jaccard 0.017
contradicting_evidence: synthetic random tokens maximize content change; the recurrence probe (S17) shows the rotation is content-driven, so 'fast' means 'changes when content changes', not 'cannot persist'
paper_safe_wording: Within synthetic packed contexts the dominant population rotates on the token timescale; there is no evidence of slow temporal specialization in this sample.
next_test: E3 frozen-corpus lag analysis; text with repeated structure (copy/retrieval probes) at inference

claim_text: A stable global core plus a small conditional tail describes the population better than either pure static or pure dynamic: the cross-fitted global top-6.25% of coordinates carries 0.614 of u mass (0.402 of x), is active in ~99.6% of tokens, and after removing it only ~34 additional coordinates (u; 158 for x) carry 50% of the residual; residual top-64 carries 0.883 of residual u mass.
dataset: latest checkpoint; core defined per (level,head) from the other batch split; per-token residual measured on 4096 tokens/level
metric: core mass fraction, core activation rate, residual top-N ratio, coordinates for 50% residual
effect_size: core:tail mass split ~61:39 for u at 6.25% core; tail width 34 coords for half the residual
uncertainty: level/head spread in core_tail.json; sensitivity across core definitions (1%, 6.25%, 25% mass-top and p_act>=0.5/0.9) reported
confound_checks: core definition sensitivity: the qualitative core+tail split holds for all five definitions; p_act>=0.9 core for u is nearly empty (0.023-0.104 mass) which is itself informative
null_test: random-init control has core-like concentration much weaker (N_eff/K 0.52 vs 0.21 for u)
contradicting_evidence: core is defined from the same sampled population it is evaluated on (cross-fitted by batch, but still in-distribution); E3 needed; the oracle ablation (S19/S20) shows the core is a descriptive hierarchy and prior, not an always-on allocation (see S23)
paper_safe_wording: The learned sparse population is consistent with a stable always-on backbone plus a narrow, context-selected specialist tail.
next_test: hybrid architecture test: always-on core + routed specialists vs equal-compute static routing

claim_text: The u conditional-mass gap is not a level-0 or boundary artifact: it appears at every layer and head, at document starts (delta 0.101 at N=64), mid-document, and in all three packed-data modes; document-level ICC of the u gap is 0.31-0.42.
dataset: latest checkpoint, stratified token meta (doc-relative position, sequence position, doc length, mode)
metric: stratified mean deltas with bootstrap CIs
effect_size: delta at N=64 ranges 0.083-0.129 (x) and 0.245-0.304 (u per-cell at N=16 ranges)
uncertainty: bootstrap CIs in position_confounds.json
confound_checks: early positions have slightly LARGER gaps, so boundary effects would if anything inflate the result only at doc starts where n=15
null_test: mode comparison (single-doc vs packed) shows nearly identical deltas
contradicting_evidence: only 15 documents were sampled for the ICC estimate
paper_safe_wording: The conditional component is present across positions, layers, heads and packing modes in the synthetic sample.
next_test: E3 with document-level resampling across many documents

claim_text: Arm-A x coordinates are strongly frequency-band organized: per-(level,head) band mass profiles are non-uniform at z=8.6-60.9 against a 5000-draw pair-preserving permutation null (32/32 cells z>3); the pooled x profile has max band share 0.229 vs null 0.143 (z=+13.2). Canonical init is exactly uniform (z=-0.2).
dataset: latest checkpoint, per-pair mass vectors over 32768 tokens per (level,head); null preserves RoPE pairs and all per-pair values
metric: band mass share non-uniformity (max share), entropy deficit, per-cell max-share z
effect_size: pooled max-share z=+13.2; entropy z=-65.1; per-cell z max 60.9
uncertainty: 5000 permutations; per-cell z in frequency_null.json
confound_checks: head identity is the main structure: H0/H3 are fast-dominant, H1 slow-dominant, H2 mid-band; the pooled profile mixes them
null_test: pair-preserving permutation; canonical-init control
contradicting_evidence: there is no universal fast/slow direction; the monotone pooled trend is driven by H0/H3
paper_safe_wording: Each attention head develops a significantly non-uniform RoPE-band profile; the direction is head-specific and absent at initialization.
next_test: frequency-band routing (top-r bands per token/head) at matched active compute

claim_text: For u=x*y the aggregate frequency organization is weak: pooled max band share 0.143 vs null 0.141 (z=+0.26); entropy z=-4.6; only 12/32 cells exceed z>3, although head 1 reaches z=27.8 at late levels.
dataset: same as S8
metric: same as S8 for key u
uncertainty: 5000 permutations
confound_checks: the u signal is concentrated in specific (level,head) cells rather than pooled
null_test: pair-preserving permutation
contradicting_evidence: per-token slow-band u mass fraction is 0.374, so slow bands are not negligible in u even if the band profile is only mildly structured
paper_safe_wording: Frequency organization is robust for x and cell-specific for u; it should not be described as a single global frequency law.
next_test: per-head band-routed u experiments; E3 replication

claim_text: The global importance hierarchy of u is dominated by the attention/LN path y, not by x: Spearman(global u mass, global y mass)=0.81-0.91 per level, while Spearman(u, x)=0.02-0.22.
dataset: latest checkpoint, per-coordinate global mass vectors per level (K=4096)
metric: Spearman rank correlation between global mass vectors
uncertainty: single vector per level; bootstrap not computed (rank correlations on 4096 coordinates)
confound_checks: y has different marginal sparsity, which can inflate rank correlations of magnitude-like quantities; still the contrast with x is large
null_test: x-y rho is negative (-0.28 to -0.47), showing the two pathways carry different hierarchies
contradicting_evidence: per-token conditional-gap correlations are only moderately different (x-u 0.54, y-u 0.59 at N=64)
paper_safe_wording: The stable coordinate hierarchy in the multiplicative path tracks the recurrent attention pathway rather than the feed-forward x projection.
next_test: store y top-N identity sets to decompose u's conditional component exactly

claim_text: The apparent '98.6% of x mass in the top quarter of coordinates' from the internal Arm-A diagnostic is a sampling artifact of measuring only 2-16 early tokens; on 4096 tokens per level the cross-fitted global top-quarter captures 0.787 of x mass and the per-token top quarter captures 0.988.
dataset: old results/sparsity_census_step19074_synth.json (2 rows, sample_rows=16 -> only 2 tokens) vs new pass1/pass2 capture (4096 tokens/level)
metric: M_local(1024) and M_global(1024) per head
uncertainty: old value had no uncertainty and was dominated by the first two tokens of the batch
confound_checks: the old u 'top-25% mass = 0.5' was even more clearly broken (total-mass denominator aliasing, zero-mass early tokens)
null_test: uniform 0.25
contradicting_evidence: the per-token local number 0.988 is close to the old 0.986, so the old number was accidentally right about per-token concentration but wrong about its scope
paper_safe_wording: Top-quarter concentration is a per-token property (0.99), not a global one (0.79); the two must not be conflated.
next_test: E3 census with the corrected sampler

claim_text: The old diagnostic's u top-25% mass share of ~0.5 was a measurement bug (denominator aliasing plus zero-mass early tokens), not a property of u.

effect_size: corrected per-token u top-256 share ~0.988, top-64 ~0.784
uncertainty: n/a

null_test: none needed for a bug
contradicting_evidence: none

claim_text: Arm-A population-level mass inequality (x Gini 0.776, u 0.828; N_eff/N 0.261/0.185) is LESS extreme than the Anthropic public feature activation-density distribution (Gini 0.926, N_eff/N 0.057, top-1% = 53.6% of density) and much more extreme than Gemma Scope encoder weight norms (Gini 0.23-0.30).
evidence_class: E1 cross-system (static reference data + E2 Arm-A)
dataset: Arm-A latest (synthetic); Gemma small/medium encoder norms; Anthropic monosemantic_2023 density (2.15M features)
metric: Gini, N_eff/N, top-share curves; each entry states its own denominator and semantics
effect_size: Gini ordering: Anthropic density 0.926 > Arm-A u 0.828 > Arm-A x 0.776 > Gemma enc norm^2 0.30
uncertainty: external files are population-level (no sampling CI needed); Arm-A side is E2
confound_checks: quantities are not the same measurement (mass vs frequency vs weight energy); comparison is explicitly dimensionless only
null_test: uniform reference lines included in figures
contradicting_evidence: Arm-A mass includes magnitude while Anthropic density is frequency-only; a like-for-like comparison (Arm-A p_act, Gini 0.53) makes Arm-A look even less sparse
paper_safe_wording: Arm-A's learned population is comparably or less concentrated than established sparse-feature dictionaries in the one dimension where they can be compared without unit confusion.
next_test: activation-frequency census of Arm-A on the frozen corpus (E3) for an exact like-for-like

claim_text: Gemma Scope l12 16k SAEs: decoder rows are exactly unit-normalized; encoder directions are much more coherent than chance (median nearest-neighbor cosine 0.475 small / 0.502 medium; mutual-NN rate 0.23/0.19) with a small duplicate tail (0.11%/0.20% of features with NN cosine >0.9); encoder effective rank 182/640 (small) and 164/640 (medium).
dataset: data/sae/gemma-scope-2-270m-pt mlp_out layer 12 width 16k small (L0=20) and medium (L0=60), widths verified against the local hash manifest
metric: norm distributions, exact NN cosine (chunked), mutual NN, spectrum
uncertainty: none needed for exact weight statistics
confound_checks: decoder unit-norm convention makes decoder-norm inequality undefined; reported explicitly
null_test: random-pair cosine distribution (std 0.072 vs 1/sqrt(640)=0.0395) shows subspace concentration
contradicting_evidence: encoder norm Gini and threshold-norm correlation change between L0 settings (0.111->0.149; -0.017->+0.401), so not all structure is L0-stable
paper_safe_wording: Gemma SAE feature geometry is low-rank and coherent, with a handful of near-duplicate features; this is structural reference data, not activation sparsity.
next_test: decode a matched hidden-state sample against both dictionaries (requires Gemma inference; out of scope)

metric: n/a

claim_text: The core+conditional-tail structure is intrinsic to the trained weights, not an artifact of the 2048-token window regime: with identically designed packed batches at T=256/512/1024/2048, Delta_u(64)=0.424/0.420/0.419/0.421, core (top-6.25%) u mass fraction=0.606/0.616/0.619/0.615, pooled band z=13.44/13.45/13.45/13.42, and top-64 stability is unchanged.
dataset: latest checkpoint; T in {256,512,1024,2048}; packed batches with exponential doc lengths mean 0.7*T, same seeds; 16 windows per T
metric: Delta_u(64) mean over 32 (level,head) cells; core mass fraction; pooled pair-preserving band z; top-64 Jaccard
effect_size: max-min across T: Delta_u 0.005, core mass 0.013, band z 0.03
uncertainty: per-cell ranges in context_length.json; per-T position strata all within 0.41-0.45
confound_checks: position strata within each T show no trend reversal; E2 raw T=2048 cross-check reproduces 0.4215/0.6143 exactly
null_test: pair-preserving permutation per T (2000 draws); cross-document stability control
contradicting_evidence: shorter T reduces maximum document length and distinct contexts per window; invariance is therefore strong but does not replace frozen-corpus testing
paper_safe_wording: The conditional component and the core are stable across evaluation context lengths from 256 to 2048 tokens on synthetic packed windows.
next_test: E3 corpus census at T=1024/2048 (e3_census.py --context)

claim_text: The tail rotation is content-driven, not positional: with a planted repeated motif, top-64 population identity persists across repetitions far above a matched shuffled control (u: 0.542/0.466/0.404 at lags 256/512/1024 vs 0.096/0.092/0.089; x: 0.62/0.56/0.51 vs ~0.13), at every level including deep layers.
dataset: latest checkpoint; T=2048 single-document windows with a 256-token base block repeated 8x (4 rows) and a shuffled control with identical unigram multiset
metric: mean top-64 Jaccard between aligned positions in different copies vs the same positions in the shuffled control; 32 offsets per row
effect_size: u repeat-minus-shuffle = +0.45/+0.37/+0.32 at lags 256/512/1024; Spearman repeat 0.945 vs shuffle 0.850
uncertainty: 32 cells per category (4 heads x 8 levels); level-resolved means in semantic_stability.json
confound_checks: level-0 x is trivially 1.0 (token identity) and reported separately; effect persists at L4-L7 (u L7 0.305 vs 0.118)
null_test: matched shuffled control (same tokens, same positions, no repetition) and cross-row pairs
contradicting_evidence: overlap decays with repetition distance (0.54->0.40 for u), so persistence is not unlimited; natural-text timescale still requires E3
paper_safe_wording: The conditional tail follows content recurrence: repeated contexts re-activate overlapping populations even when intervening tokens differ, so the fast rotation measured on random tokens reflects content change rather than position noise.
next_test: E3 semantic recurrence on frozen-corpus documents (sentence/document strata, lags 1-256)

claim_text: The core/tail decomposition has a stable operating region rather than one threshold: across core fractions 1/3.125/6.25/12.5/25% of K, u core mass is 0.294/0.480/0.614/0.753/0.879, and total active width needed for 90% of u mass is minimized at the 3.125-6.25% core (5.6-8.3% of K per head).
dataset: latest checkpoint; dedicated cross-fitted ladder run (raw/raw_ladder), residual quantiles 50/80/90%
metric: per-token core mass fraction; coordinates for 50/80/90% of residual; coverage at matched width
uncertainty: p10-p90 per cell in core_ladder.json
confound_checks: p_act-based core definitions behave differently (u core mass 0.19-0.40 for p_act>=0.5), confirming mass-based cores are the right family
null_test: uniform coverage reference
contradicting_evidence: x has no narrow core; its 90% width is 15-31% of K, so the operating-region statement is u-specific
paper_safe_wording: A 3-6% always-on core plus a routed tail is the efficient operating region for the multiplicative path.
next_test: E4 arm matrix should include core fractions 3.125% and 6.25% rather than only 6.25%

claim_text: Forward-only oracle ablation falsifies the prediction hybrid<dynamic<static in output fidelity: at 320 active coordinates/head, oracle-dynamic keeps 98.9% of u mass (4.0% relative logit perturbation), hybrid 91.2% (24.2%), static 51.1% (83.3%); zeroing all u perturbs logits by 55.9%.
dataset: latest checkpoint, 8 held-out packed windows (batch split B); frozen u-mass rankings from split A; masking applied at every level
metric: mean per-token relative L2 logit perturbation vs dense forward; u mass kept
effect_size: dynamic 320 is 21x closer to dense than static 320 and 6x closer than hybrid
uncertainty: two evaluation batches; per-batch values recorded
confound_checks: static ranking and core are cross-fitted; widths exactly matched at 320 coordinates/head
null_test: zero-u mutation (upper reference) and dense baseline
contradicting_evidence: dynamic/hybrid select using the true u activations (oracle); a learned router will be worse, so the E4 training comparison is still required
paper_safe_wording: At matched active width, oracle per-token selection preserves the model output far better than a frozen global selection; the fixed-core hybrid is a cost compromise, not a fidelity optimum.
next_test: E4 with a learned router (router_recall@k) and all three arms

claim_text: Static-only expertization is not viable for the u path of this checkpoint: a frozen global top-320 keeps only 51% of per-token u mass and perturbs the output by 83% relative to dense.

uncertainty: per-batch spread recorded

null_test: zero-u mutation 0.559 perturbation is LOWER than static-320, showing static masking can damage the output more than removing u entirely
contradicting_evidence: static selection is harmless at very large widths (>=2048), but that removes the compute advantage
paper_safe_wording: Global static coordinate selection cannot substitute for context-dependent selection in the multiplicative path.
next_test: E4 static arm must be reported as the negative control

claim_text: The stable core is descriptive population structure and a useful prior (router prior, initialization bias, fallback population, capacity reservation, regularization target), not evidence that forcing the core always-on is the optimal compute allocation.
dataset: S19/S20 forward-only oracle ablation at matched width
metric: fidelity ranking at 320 coords/head: oracle dynamic 4.0% vs hybrid 24.2% vs static 83.3%
